summary: The Verge's Antonio G. Di Benedetto rounds up the best Xbox controllers for Xbox Series X/S and Windows PC, concluding the standard Xbox Wireless Controller is best for most people. He picks alternatives for budget, premium, customization and shooters, weighing connectivity, quality, extra features, customization and value.
one_line: The Verge ranks the best Xbox controllers, naming the standard Xbox Wireless Controller best overall, with picks for budget, premium, customization and shooters.
key_facts: The standard Xbox Wireless Controller is the best Xbox controller for most people; it has a Share button, Bluetooth, USB-C and runs on AA batteries or an add-on rechargeable pack.
The Xbox Wireless Controller is the only affordable wireless Xbox controller thanks to Microsoft's proprietary protocol, and Xbox Design Lab customization costs $69.99 to $99.94.
The PowerA Enhanced Wired Controller is the best cheap pick: $37.99 retail (some colors around $25), Micro USB, two mappable rear buttons, no impulse trigger rumble, and a two-year warranty.
PowerA's Advantage Wired Controller is a newer version of the Enhanced with USB-C and hair-trigger lockouts, but at $37.99 it can't match the Enhanced's near-perpetual discounts.
The PowerA Fusion Pro 3 costs $79.99, is $10 cheaper than its predecessor and lighter, with four rear buttons, trigger lockouts and rubberized grips as a wired Elite alternative.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 is the best premium pick: normally $179.99 (sometimes $139.99), with up to four rear paddles, software customization, built-in rechargeable battery and a charging dock and case, but no Share button.

The Elite Series 2 Core costs $129.99 without paddles, case or extra toppers; the $59.99 accessories pack makes it $10 more than a standard Elite Series 2, and the Design Lab 'Elite Package' costs $209.99.
Microsoft extended the Elite Series 2 warranty from 90 days to a year in late 2020 after quality-control complaints.

The Scuf Instinct Pro starts at $199.99 (the tested one cost $263.91), is the only third-party wireless option, has four rocker-style rear buttons and the fastest hair triggers, but uses AA batteries and lacks software customization.

RIG's Nacon Revolution X is the best customizable controller at $99.99 wired, with four rear buttons, four user profiles, a classic mode, Dolby Atmos for Headphones license, ring spacers and 10g to 16g grip weights.

The Turtle Beach Recon is the best for shooters at about $60 (once as low as $39.95), with Superhuman Hearing audio mode, two rear buttons and Pro Aim sensitivity adjustment, but a cheap-feeling plastic build.
